label: Discord
terms_note: Free; a bot application + bot token (Authorization: Bot …) invited to the user's server with SEND_MESSAGES / VIEW_CHANNEL / READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY; the MESSAGE_CONTENT privileged intent is needed to read message text (empty content / embeds / attachments otherwise) and needs verification once the bot is in 100+ servers; global limit 50 requests/s plus per-route buckets (X-RateLimit-* headers, 429 with retry_after); automating USER accounts (self-bots) is prohibited by the Developer Policy — bots only.

sdks: discord.py / discord.js / JDA (community, endorsed in the docs)

auth: 1. Developer Portal → application → Bot → token (`Authorization: Bot <token>`); OAuth2 invite URL with `bot` scope and
2. Privileged intents: `MESSAGE_CONTENT` (1 << 15) to read message text; verification required once the bot is in
3. Channel webhooks (`POST /channels/{id}/webhooks`) allow posting without a gateway session.
reference.limits: - Global 50 requests/s per bot; per-route buckets via `X-RateLimit-Limit / -Remaining / -Reset-After`, 429 body `retry_after`; invalid-request cap 10,000 / 10 min. - Free. Developer Policy: no self-bots / automated user accounts, no unsolicited DMs or spam, data use limited to the app's function; message content only with the intent.

fields.name: bot_token
fields.help: Bot token from the app's Bot page in the Developer Portal, pasted WITHOUT the 'Bot ' prefix: the runtime adds it and sends 'Authorization: Bot <token>' ('authentication is performed with the Authorization HTTP header in the format Authorization: TOKEN_TYPE TOKEN', https://docs.discord.com/developers/reference#authentication). Channel permissions needed: VIEW_CHANNEL + READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY (read_comments), SEND_MESSAGES (publish_text, reply_comment), MANAGE_MESSAGES to delete other users' messages; the MESSAGE_CONTENT privileged intent to read other users' message content. Same field as the messaging entry (env PLATFORM_MCP_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN).

config_fields.name: channel_id
config_fields.help: Snowflake id of the guild text / announcement channel (or forum-post thread) the bot publishes to (Discord client: User Settings > Advanced > Developer Mode, then right-click the channel > Copy Channel ID). The social vocabulary carries no channel argument, so publish_text, reply_comment and delete all address /channels/<channel_id>/messages; env PLATFORM_MCP_DISCORD_CHANNEL_ID.

adapter.rate_note: 'All bots can make up to 50 requests per second to our API' globally, plus per-route buckets announced in X-RateLimit-Limit / -Remaining / -Reset / -Reset-After / -Bucket and enforced with 429 + Retry-After (https://docs.discord.com/developers/topics/rate-limits). Per-route numbers are not published, so the client bucket stays at the runtime default 2/s.
adapter.user_agent_note: Discord asks HTTP clients for a User-Agent 'in the following format: DiscordBot ($url, $versionNumber)' (https://docs.discord.com/developers/reference#user-agent); the runtime sends its own 'platform-mcp/discord (+url)' User-Agent, which is a valid but non-canonical value (UNCONFIRMED whether Discord ever rejects it).

me.note: GET /users/@me 'Returns the user object of the requester's account' - for a bot token the bot's own user (id, username, discriminator, global_name, bot: true).

publish_text.note: POST /channels/{channel.id}/messages ('Post a message to a guild text or DM channel') into the configured channel_id; `text` is `content` ('Message contents (up to 2000 characters)'). `reply_to` (a message id in the same channel) is sent as message_reference.message_id ('Replies are created by including a message_reference when sending a message. The referenced message must exist or the request will fail with HTTP error 400' - an upstream_error). Returns the message object: `id` is the message id, which identifies the post only together with the channel it lives in (delete uses the configured channel_id); `created_at` is the ISO-8601 `timestamp`; Discord messages carry no url. Needs SEND_MESSAGES (plus READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY for replies).

read_comments.note: `post_id` is a CHANNEL or THREAD id, not a message id: Discord has no per-message reply list, but a thread is addressed like a channel and a thread started from a message shares that message's id ('The id of the created thread will be the same as the id of the source message, and as such a message can only have a single thread created from it', https://docs.discord.com/developers/resources/channel#start-thread-from-message), so passing a forum post's id (or any thread id) lists the replies in that thread; passing a text channel id lists the channel. GET /channels/{channel.id}/messages: 'Retrieves the messages in a channel. Returns an array of message objects from newest to oldest on success.' `limit` is 'Max number of messages to return (1-100)', default 50; Discord pages by message id (before / after / around), so `page` is ignored and only the newest `limit` messages are returned. Needs VIEW_CHANNEL + READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY ('If the current user is missing the READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY permission in the channel, then no messages will be returned'), and other users' `content` is empty without the MESSAGE_CONTENT intent. `author` is author.username (id under raw.author.id).

reply_comment.note: A reply is a Create Message carrying message_reference.message_id = comment_id ('Replies are created by including a message_reference when sending a message'), posted into the configured channel_id - so the comment must live in that channel (message_reference.channel_id is not sent, and 'The referenced message must exist or the request will fail with HTTP error 400'). Needs SEND_MESSAGES + READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY.

delete.note: DELETE /channels/{channel.id}/messages/{message.id} deletes the message `post_id` in the configured channel_id: 'Delete a message. The current user must be the author of the message or, if the message was in a guild channel, have the MANAGE_MESSAGES permission. Returns a 204 No Content response on success.' The runtime answers {status: 'deleted'}; a message that is not in the configured channel is a 404 (invalid_input).

publish_image.note: Create Message with `embeds` ('Up to 10 rich embeds'; 'at least one of content, embeds, files, sticker_ids, poll, or components' is required) into the configured channel_id: each image URL becomes one embed whose `image.url` is 'source url of image (only supports http(s) and attachments)' (Embed Image Structure {url, proxy_url?, height?, width?}); `text` is the message `content`. Up to FOUR image_urls are sent (embeds 0-3; more are ignored) - Discord itself must be able to fetch the URLs. Same response mapping as publish_text (id, created_at = timestamp; no url).

not_offered.read_mentions: No REST mention feed exists for bots: mentions arrive only as Gateway MESSAGE_CREATE events over the WebSocket connection (https://docs.discord.com/developers/events/gateway-events#message-create), which the HTTP runtime does not hold.
not_offered.analytics_post: Discord publishes no view / impression metrics for a message; Get Channel Message returns only a per-emoji `reactions` array ({count, emoji, ...}) and no aggregate counters (https://docs.discord.com/developers/resources/message#get-channel-message).
